$comment: Gzipped byte ceilings per compiled file, checked by bin/check-asset-budget.js on every build. The first matching rule wins; an asset that matches no rule fails the build. The JavaScript and block CSS ceilings come from the performance budgets G9 and G10. Those budgets are per template, so a per-file ceiling equal to them is the loosest bound that can still catch a regression; the Playwright byte fixture enforces the per-template totals and reads this file rather than restating the numbers. The admin CSS ceiling is a starting value to calibrate against the first real screen. Raising any ceiling is a reviewed change that says why.
